title: Assessing Budding Yeast Phosphoproteome Dynamics Using TMT10plex Mass Tag Labeling
author: Jones, Flynn, et al.
materials: Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid Mass Spectrometer

steps.title: Grow and synchronize yeast cultures
steps.instruction: Perform a two‑day culture and synchronization of control and mutant Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains expressing GAL1‑controlled CDC20.

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Inoculate 400 ml YP medium containing 2 % galactose and 2 % raffinose with control and mutant cells and grow for 16 h at 25 °C.
Morning of Day 2: Back‑dilute cultures to OD₆₀₀ = 0.1 (≈1.5 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹) in the same YP + 2 % galactose + 2 % raffinose medium and continue growth at 25 °C.

When OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.2 (≈3 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹), filter the cells, wash with 3 l YP medium lacking galactose, and grow for 3 h in YP medium containing 2 % raffinose at 25 °C to achieve metaphase arrest via Cdc20 depletion.
Allow cultures to reach OD₆₀₀ = 0.3–0.4 (≈4.5–6 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹). Collect 25 ml as the first time point (t = 0) just before galactose re‑addition and process immediately (see Extract Preparation).
Add 2 % galactose to both strains to re‑induce Cdc20 expression, permitting synchronous progression through mitosis. At the end of the experiment add 0.8 µg ml⁻¹ α‑factor to re‑arrest cells in G1.
Collect additional samples at t = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 60 and 90 min from both control and mutant cultures and process each immediately.
Use a stock solution of 20 % galactose and 20 % raffinose for all galactose/raffinose additions.

steps.title: Prepare protein extracts
steps.instruction: Harvest cells, precipitate proteins with TCA, wash, and lyse in amine‑free urea buffer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge each 25 ml sample at 2000 g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 ml ice‑cold 20 % TCA, vortex, and keep on ice for at least 1 h.
Aspirate the TCA, then wash the pellet twice with 10 ml cold acetone (‑20 °C). After the final wash, allow any residual acetone to evaporate completely.

Resuspend the pellet in 400 µl lysis buffer composed of 8 M urea, 50 mM HEPES pH 8.2, 5 mM EDTA, 1 mM dithiothreitol, 50 mM sodium fluoride, 1 mM sodium vanadate, 1 mM PMSF, and a cOmplete™ EDTA‑Free Protease Inhibitor Cocktail.
Transfer the suspension to a 2 ml Eppendorf tube suitable for a Fast‑Prep cell breaker.
Add 500 µl acid‑washed glass beads, then beat on the Fast‑Prep at 6.0 m s⁻¹ for 4 × 40 s cycles in the cold room, keeping the lid closed between cycles.
Inspect a small aliquot by phase‑contrast microscopy to confirm efficient cell breakage (intact cells appear bright, broken cells dark).
Punch a hole in the bottom of each cell‑breaker tube with a heated hypodermic needle, place the tube into a 15 ml centrifuge tube, and collect the lysate by brief centrifugation.
Transfer the lysate to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 16 000 g for 10 min.
Measure protein concentration in the supernatant with a Protein Assay Dye; the concentration must be > 500 µg ml⁻¹.
Aliquot the amount corresponding to 200 µg protein into LoBind microcentrifuge tubes and store at –80 °C (pause point; samples can be kept indefinitely).

steps.title: Prepare samples for LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Resuspend extracts, clean up, and inject into the nano‑LC‑MS system.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each 200 µg protein aliquot in 35 µl 1 % trifluoroacetic acid (TFA).
Sonicate the suspension for 15 min, then centrifuge at 14 000 rpm, 4 °C for 5 min.
Transfer the cleared supernatant to Total Recovery glass autosampler vials.
Perform triplicate injections of each sample (10 µl per injection).
Set the nanoLC flow rate to 250 nl min⁻¹ and run the following gradient:
0–5 min: 2 % mobile phase B
Mobile phase A = 95 % H₂O, 5 % DMSO, 0.1 % formic acid; Mobile phase B = 75 % acetonitrile, 5 % DMSO, 20 % H₂O, 0.1 % formic acid.
MS acquisition settings:
Full MS (Orbitrap, 120 000 resolution): scan range 350–1500 m/z, AGC target 4.0 × 10⁵, maximum injection time 50 ms, data‑dependent cycle time 3 s.

MS/MS (Orbitrap, 60 000 resolution): HCD with 38 % collision energy, isolation window 0.7 m/z, first mass 100 m/z, AGC target 1.0 × 10⁵, maximum injection time 105 ms, charge states 2–7, dynamic exclusion 45 s after 1 count.

steps.title: Process raw data with MaxQuant and Perseus
steps.instruction: Identify and quantify phosphopeptides, then import results into Perseus for statistical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Download the current S. cerevisiae proteome FASTA from UniProt.
In MaxQuant, define the two TMT‑10plex mixes as separate experiment groups and run the standard workflow (Andromeda search).
After MaxQuant finishes, locate the file phosphoSTY.txt and open it in Perseus.
Import the TMT reporter ion intensities as expression values.
Select the desired phosphosite multiplicity (e.g., singly phosphorylated).
Remove entries originating from the decoy and contaminant databases.
Apply a log₂ transformation to all reporter ion intensity values.
Normalize each column (sample) by subtracting its median value to correct for mixing errors.
Add categorical annotations to label the two multiplexed pools and to indicate the yeast strain for each sample.
Filter the dataset to retain phosphosites that have at least ten valid values in at least one multiplexed pool.

steps.title: Quantify and analyze phosphosite dynamics
steps.instruction: Perform median subtraction, imputation, smoothing, and deposit data.

substeps.instruction: For each phosphorylation site, subtract the median value of that site within each multiplexed pool (or use an equivalent normalization).
Impute any missing value by averaging the two adjacent time points (t‑1 and t + 1).
Smooth the time‑course by averaging each data point with its adjacent t‑1 and t + 1 values.
Deposit the final dataset to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE repository (Project ID: PXD012860).
